Our Company:

At impact.com we’re passionate about our people and our technology, and are obsessed with customer success. Working together helps us to grow rapidly, to win, and to serve the largest brands in the world. 

We transform the way our clients manage, track, optimise and measure all types of partnerships, including traditional affiliates, influencers, commerce content publishers, B2B, and more. 

Our powerful, purpose-built platform makes it easy for businesses to scale an ecosystem of partnerships with the brands and communities their customers trust to make purchases, get information, and entertain themselves at home, at work, or on the go. 

We have an entrepreneurial spirit and a culture where ambition and curiosity is rewarded. If you are looking to join a team where your opinion is valued, your contributions are noticed, and you enjoy working with fun and talented people from all over the world, then this could be the place for you!

Your Role at impact.com:

The Channel Partnership Manager ANZ is responsible for the overall growth of impact.com’s agencies and tech partners in the region and for building and maintaining effective commercial relationships to achieve and exceed targeted pipeline and revenue goals.

You will manage inbound and outbound agency referrals, drive growth and adoption of the impact.com Agency partner program, deliver agency onboarding, education, in market training and enablement and business reviews. 

You’re a key conduit between our Agency and Tech partners and the go-to-market Sales and Marketing teams and a liaison to our Customer Success and Publisher Development teams. This role is fundamental to the success of the go-to-market sales team, driving primarily new customer logos as well as growth from existing customers via cross-sell opportunities, and upgrades.

Our ambition is to expand the partnership ecosystem by deeply understanding our customers’ needs,  providing true business value and working together for long term partnership success. 

We are looking for a self starter with the motivation and drive to become elite. A growth mindset and coachability are essential for success at impact.com.

What You'll Do:

Plan and execute within your assigned territory of agency and partner accounts, driving a balanced approach across SMB, Mid-Market and Enterprise level prospects. 

Meet and exceed individual pipeline and bookings targets through new prospects and by growing existing customers

Master the lead indicators of the impact.com sales process such as generating minimum visible pipeline, accurate forecasting, driving value alignment with agencies, partners and prospects and securing win:win commercial outcomes

Have the ability to navigate and manage short, medium and complex long term sales-cycles with a range of different personas within agencies, technical partners and with prospects as required.  

Be a highly effective communicator and stakeholder manager and have the ability to plan ahead to deliver required outcomes 

Develop and implement channel partner programs for agency and tech partners including marketing initiatives, events, lunch and learns and workshops

Execute all impact.com systems and tools to the highest standard, ensuring customer records are timely and complete

Have a commitment to consistently building own knowledge base around the performance marketing and partnerships ecosystem and impact.com’s role within it 

Other duties as assigned by the Company

What You Have:

Must have at least 3+ years successful commercial experience with evidence of consistent performance and target attainment within a sales / SaaS organisation 

1+ years minimum experience working with agencies and technical partners

A network of agency contacts would be advantageous  

Digital marketing, particularly performance / affiliate marketing ecosystem knowledge preferred 

Understanding of sales methodologies such as MEDDPICC 

Experience with sales and outbound communication tools (such as Salesforce, Salesloft etc) 

Have a customer orientation and desire to see customer success for the long term 

Demonstrable positive attitude, individual drive and persistence 

Have exceptional problem-solving, objection handling, networking and presentation skills

Be curious, tenacious and resilient with a growth mindset and coachability 

A team player who fosters collaboration through open communication and takes personal ownership and accountability

listings.description:
impact.comについて

impact.comは、ビジネスの成長を変革するグローバルをリードするコマースパートナーシップマーケティングプラットフォームです。アフィリエイト、クリエイター/インフルエンサー、コンテンツパブリッシャー、ブランドアンバサダー、カスタマーアドボケートなど、様々なタイプのパートナーをリクルートし、スケールをもった管理のもと、ユーザージャーニー全体にわたる信頼性の高い成果ベースの成長を実現します。ソリューションは、Performance（アフィリエイト）、Creator（インフルエンサー）、Advocate（顧客紹介）といった受賞歴のあるラインアップを提供し、多岐にわたるパートナーマーケティングを1つの統合プラットフォームで活用することが可能です。ユーザーが信頼できるソースやコミュニティからの推奨に大きな影響をうけるこの時代だからこそ、impact.comは効果的な形ででブランドを際立たせるためのサポートを行っています。現在、Walmart、Uber、Shopify、Lenovo、L'Oréal、Fantasticsを含む6,000以上のグローバルや国内ブランドが、impact.comを利用して数十万のパートナーシップを管理し、成果ベースの成果を日々もたらしています。

本ロールの役割:

クリエイター・コンサルティング+リレーション・マネージャーとして、戦略的ブランドコンサルティングとクリエイター/インフルエンサーマネージメントを橋渡しすることで、APJチームの一員としてクリエイターエコノミーの加速において重要な役割を果たしていただきます。単にリレーションシップを管理するのではなく、エキスパートアドボケートとして、クリエイター/インフルエンサーと世界的なトップブランドを含めたクライアントがパフォーマンス主導型のパートナーシップにおける収益を最大化できるように努めていただきます。本ロールはコミュニティ構築を得意とし、データドリブンマーケティングに長け、急成長をしているマーケットでパートナーシップコマースを構築して大きなインパクトを残すことにやりがいを感じていただける方に最適なロールです。

本ロールに行っていただくこと:

広告主に対して、パフォーマンスクリエイター/インフルエンサー戦略を設計・実行し、キャンペーン設計やKPI（ROASなど）に対する提案〜実行まで行います。

クリエイター/インフルエンサーのリクルーティングからオンボーディングをリード し、impact.comプラットフォーム上のエクスペリエンスを通じて、パートナーの成長に寄与できるようにします。

クリエイター/インフルエンサーリレーションを育成し、コミュニケーション、積極的なサポート、コミュニティ構築を行い、信頼できる成長パートナーとして機能します。

戦略的提案を提供し、クリエイター/インフルエンサーとブランドパートナーにキャンペーンの最適化とベストプラクティスに関するアクションドリブンなインサイトを提供します。

キャンペーンのインサイトを分析・共有し、転換率、エンゲージメント、ROIなど主要KPIをトラッキングし、インセンティブ戦略やキャンペーンの最適化を継続的に行います。

クリエイター/インフルエンサーエクスペリエンスをサポートし、パートナーからのフィードバックを積極的に活用し、プラットフォームの継続的な改善を行います。

必須スキル/経験:

クリエイター/インフルエンサーマーケティング、アフィリエイトマーケティング、またはコミュニティ管理における4年以上の経験および大規模なクリエイター/インフルエンサープログラムをマネージした実績。

ソーシャルメディアの業界知識およびパフォーマンスマーケティングにおけるクリエイター/インフルエンサーの活用モデルについての深い理解とインサイト。

適切なコミュニケーションスキルやウェビナーやワークショップなど効果的なチャネル活動に対する経験やモチベーション、その他複雑なアイデアをアクションに落とし込む実行力。

データドリブンなマインドセットを持ち、パフォーマンスに対する最適なアクションをリードしていくスキル。

積極的かつ協力的であり、戦略的プログラムの設計と実行を両立させるために、アジャイル環境で自律的に行動をし、それを成長モチベーションとして捉える姿勢。

プラスとなるスキル/経験:

SaaS、テックプラットフォーム、またはデジタルマーケティング（エージェンシー）の経験。

クリエイター/インフルエンサー業界、ソーシャルトレンド、成果ベースのパフォーマンスマーケティングに対する情熱。

福利厚生を含むベネフィット:

impact.comでは、ワークライフバランスに加え、メンバーの成長をサポートする福利厚生パッケージを提供しています。

フレキシブルな勤務形態：当社の有休ポリシーは、必要な時間を取ってリフレッシュできることを意味します。ワークライスバランスに配慮し、キャリアと個人生活の両方で幸福と充実を実現できる柔軟な環境を提供しています。

健康とウェルネス：従業員の満足度は優先事項です。メンタルヘルスおよびウェルネスベネフィットには、年間最大12回の完全カバーされたセラピー/コーチングセッション（配偶者のカバーオプション付き）が含まれています。また、月々のフィットネスジム料金を支払いし、心身の健康をサポートしています。

成長への投資：継続的なラーニング機会にコミットしています。無料のCourseraサブスクリプションと自社のトレーニングプログラムであるPXAコースを活用できます。

育児支援：充実した育児休暇制度を提供しており、主要な養護者には26週間の有給休暇、また二次的な養護者には13週間の完全有給休暇があります。

ハイブリッドワーク支援：ホームオフィスのセットアップに活用できる手当とインターネット料金をカバーする月額手当を提供しています。

RSU：総報酬パッケージの一部として制限付きストックユニット（RSU）を提供し、3年のベスティングスケジュール（取締役会の承認待ち）で当社の成長に参画ができます。

listings.title: Creator Marketing Consulting Manager
listings.description:
About impact.com
impact.com is the world’s leading commerce partnership marketing platform, transforming the way businesses grow by enabling them to discover, manage, and scale partnerships across the entire customer journey. From affiliates and influencers to content publishers, brand ambassadors, and customer advocates, impact.com empowers brands to drive trusted, performance-based growth through authentic relationships. Its award-winning products—Performance (affiliate), Creator (influencer), and Advocate (customer referral)—unify every type of partner into one integrated platform. As consumers increasingly rely on recommendations from people and communities they trust, impact.com helps brands show up where it matters most. Today, over 5,000 global brands, including Walmart, Uber, Shopify, Lenovo, L’Oréal, and Fanatics, rely on impact.com to power more than 225,000 partnerships that deliver measurable business results.

Your Role at impact.com:

The world’s largest advertisers are rebuilding their creator programs around performance. They no longer want campaigns alone — they want an always-on operating system: a center of excellence with the strategy, compensation model, a scaled casting engine, a new measurement framework, and the internal muscle to run it at scale.

That is what you build.

As a Creator Consulting Manager, you are a member of impact.com’s Creator Strategy practice, designing and optimizing the most sophisticated performance creator programs in the market. You work directly with brand teams and their agencies — diagnosing what they actually need beneath what they’ve asked for, translating ambiguity into roadmaps, and then standing up in front of a room and teaching others how to run it. You are equal parts strategist, economist, architect, creative, innovator, facilitator, and teacher.

This is a client-facing, high-visibility role for someone who thrives on complexity, moves fast with demanding stakeholders, and wants to help define what performance creator marketing becomes over the next five years.

What You'll Do:

Design profitable programs that scale

Build and optimize end-to-end strategies for the largest performance creator (creator-affiliate) programs in the world, from initial thesis through research, audits, launch, iteration, optimization, and expansion.

Partner with enterprise advertisers to stand up creator centers of excellence — the governance, workflows, roles, and roadmap that turn a program into an institution.

Architect compensation strategies that motivate creators: tiered gamification balanced against flat fees, commission structures, performance bonuses, loyalty program integrations, and bespoke incentives tuned to each program’s economics.

Build the creator supply engine

Develop integrated casting and recruitment strategies spanning paid, earned, and owned media, with both inbound and outbound motions.

Design scaled vetting and brand safety frameworks that let programs grow without exposing the brand.

Design creator communications strategies and workflows — the cadence, channels, and content that keep thousands of creators informed, activated, motivated, and productive.

Make the creative perform

Build creative strategies that focus on affiliate-optimized formats, translating what converts on performance rails into briefs creators can actually execute.

Bring a working point of view on social and performance media trends, and pressure-test which ones deserve client investment.

Teach and enable

Plan and facilitate workshops, trainings, and enablement sessions for brand teams and their agencies — you are the person in the room, not just the person who built the deck.

Represent impact.com externally: conference stages, client executive sessions, panels, and webinars.

Partner across Creator Strategy

Work hand-in-hand with Creator Solutions on program management and operational execution.

Partner with Creator Relations and Creator Productivity on creator onboarding, coaching, and lifecycle programming.

Feed field learning back into the practice, so what you build for one client sharpens the team’s best practices playbook.

Measure, prove, optimize

Apply advanced measurement approaches — MMM, brand lift, sales lift, and MTA — to demonstrate incremental impact and guide reinvestment.

Continuously optimize how the work gets done, using better process design and AI to compress cycle time and raise output quality.

What You Bring: 

5+ years of experience building complex, performance marketing strategies for demanding, fast-paced enterprise brands.

You’re comfortable being handed a vague directive and returning with a clear roadmap, requirements, and stakeholder alignment.

Extensive knowledge across performance marketing, affiliate marketing, and creator marketing, and fluency in the SaaS platforms that power them.

Working proficiency with leading performance creator platforms such as LTK and ShopMy.

Expert-level public speaking. You can hold a room of senior marketers and make a complicated idea land.

Expert-level workshop design and facilitation — you know the difference between presenting and facilitating, and you’re good at both.

Fluency in advanced marketing measurement: MMM, brand lift, sales lift, MTA.

Strong project management discipline across multiple concurrent, high-stakes engagements.

A process optimizer’s instinct — you notice friction and fix it rather than routing around it.

A genuine appetite for teaching. The best outcome of your work is a client team that no longer needs you in the room.

Thought leadership: you’re not just applying performance creator marketing best practice, you’re inventing it.

Nice to have:

Fluency in measurement technology and the vendor landscape behind it.

Hands-on experience with performance paid media.

Published writing, speaking, or original research in the creator or performance marketing space.

Why this role matters

impact.com sits on the affiliate rails that make performance creator marketing possible. The Creator Consulting team is how that infrastructure becomes strategy for the world’s biggest brands. You’ll shape programs that move real GTV, define methods the market hasn’t seen yet, and build the internal capability that outlasts any single campaign.

Salary range: $100,000- $110,000 + $25,000.00 - $27,500.00 Variable, plus eligibility to receive Restricted Stock Unit (RSU) grant.
*This is the pay range the Company believes is equitable for this position at the time of this posting. Consistent with applicable law, compensation will be determined based on the skills, qualifications, and experience of the applicant along with the requirements of the position, and the Company reserves the right to modify this pay range at any time.

Benefits and Perks: 

At impact.com, we believe that when you’re happy and fulfilled, you do your best work. That’s why we’ve built a benefits package that supports your well-being, growth, and work-life balance.

Flexible Working: Our Responsible PTO policy means you can take the time off you need to rest and recharge. We're committed to a positive work-life balance and provide a flexible environment that allows you to be happy and fulfilled in both your career and your personal life.

Health and Wellness: Your well-being is a priority. Our mental health and wellness benefit includes up to 12 fully covered therapy/coaching sessions per year, with additional dependent coverage. We also offer a monthly gym reimbursement policy to support your physical health.

A Stake in Our Growth: We offer Restricted Stock Units (RSUs) as part of our total compensation, giving you a stake in the company's growth with a 3-year vesting schedule, pending Board approval.

Investing in Your Growth: We’re committed to your continuous learning. Take advantage of our free Coursera subscription and our PXA courses.

Parental Support: We offer a generous parental leave policy, 26 weeks of fully paid leave for the primary caregiver and 13 weeks fully paid leave for the secondary caregiver.

Technology Financial Support: We provide a technology stipend to help you set up your home office and a monthly allowance to cover your internet expenses.

impact.com is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace. All employees and applicants for employment shall be given fair treatment and equal employment opportunity regardless of their race, ethnicity or ancestry, color or caste, religion or belief, age, sex (including gender identity, gender reassignment, sexual orientation, pregnancy/maternity), national origin, weight, neurodivergence, disability, marital and civil partnership status, caregiving status, veteran status, genetic information, political affiliation, or other prohibited non-merit factors.

impact.com, the world’s leading partnership management platform, is transforming the way businesses manage and optimize all types of partnerships—including traditional rewards affiliates, influencers, commerce content publishers, B2B, and more. Position Overview

As a member of the Creator Solutions team, impact.com’s in-house performance creator experts, you will be responsible for driving success across a portfolio of client accounts. You will manage creator programs and campaigns across diverse verticals, including fashion, parenting, food, technology, and more. Our programs span from introductory performance-led strategies to year-long brand ambassador initiatives. In this role, you will own the campaign execution cycle from start to finish for a select group of clients while providing key support on a variety of larger, strategic programs. 

Your Role at impact.com:

You will be the primary driver of growth and engagement within our clients' Creator and Affiliate Programs. This involves partnering with our brands to design, implement, and scale comprehensive strategies for creator recruitment, relationship management, and community growth, ensuring a vibrant, active, and profitable partner network.

Develop and implement performance-led strategies to attract creators aligned with defined brand and business goals.

Strategize content creation and casting to ensure campaigns are on trend and highly relevant to the current social media landscape.

Recruitment & Campaign Execution 

Lead a 360° creator recruitment effort, identifying and targeting creators to join programs/campaigns, leveraging offshore support where necessary.

Source and vet qualified creators for each campaign, providing data-driven recommendations based on follower count, location, niche, and audience demographics.

Create comprehensive creator campaign briefs based on client guidelines and FTC/disclosure compliance standards.

Client & Creator Management 

Leads  kick-off calls and prepare all necessary documentation (internal and external), efficiently responding to client communications.

Negotiate terms and communicate extensively with creators, including facilitating product orders and gathering content drafts.

Review and approve creator content to ensure compliance with the brief and quality standards (e.g., spelling and grammar).

Provide excellent customer service and subject matter expertise, ensuring client and creator satisfaction and trust in our services.

Performance & Optimization 

Monitor and manage program timelines and budgets to ensure both revenue goals and client deadlines are consistently met.

Gather campaign metrics, analyze performance, and format data to generate actionable insights.

Identify potential upselling opportunities and communicate these effectively to senior leadership.

Design and execute incentive programs, including flat fees, performance-based rewards, and exclusive offers.

Internal Collaboration 

Collaborate closely with internal teams (community support, sales, product, marketing, and client success) to ensure creator community and affiliate strategies align with overarching business goals.

What You Have:

Adventageous: Completion of your free Getting Started with Influencer Partnerships Certification on PXA. Candidates must mention this completion in their cover letter.

Fluency in Mandarin (spoken and written) is required for managing Mandarin-speaking clients and creators

Bachelor's Degree or relevant experience

At least 2-4+ years of proven professional experience in the Affiliate Marketing, Creator Marketing, or Community Management space.

Strong foundational knowledge of creator and affiliate marketing strategies, tools, and technologies.

Familiarity with the impact.com or another affiliate marketing platform is a plus.

Strong knowledge of creators across verticals, especially CPG, fashion, parenting, wellness, fitness, etc., and creator rates

Experience with niches such as gaming, tech, finance, entertainment, etc. a plus

Familiarity with the essential components of the creator lifecycle: budgeting, casting, negotiating, contracting, fulfillment oversight, draft approvals, and reporting.

Exceptional communication skills (written and verbal) with demonstrated ability to engage and motivate diverse Creators, affiliates, and clients.

A data-driven mindset with proficiency in analyzing metrics and translating them into actionable business insights.

Relationship-driven approach with the ability to manage diverse personalities and work styles.

Strong passion for and knowledge of social media platforms and the ability to adapt to sudden changes in trends and industry shifts.

Self-starter mentality with a strong drive to develop client businesses and succeed personally.

Proven ability to work independently, manage multiple priorities, and thrive in a fast-paced environment.

Strong problem-solving skills.

Demonstrate a growth mindset and a willingness to continuously learn and improve.

Benefits and Perks:

Your Role at Impact:

Impact's Data Platform Engineering team is looking for a Data Platform Engineer ready to independently own production pipelines and platform components at TB-scale, delivering data reliably, securely, and cost-effectively as the business grows.

You'll design and build scalable batch and streaming pipelines, own the reliability, performance, and SLOs of your domain, and participate fully in on-call as a Tier 2 responder. You'll work within the Data Analytics Group (DAG), partnering closely with Analytics Engineers, Data Analysts, Data Scientists, and Data Product Managers, though you won't own dbt models, metric definitions, or reporting. We operate with a platform-as-a-product mindset: the platform is an internal product with clear interfaces, paved roads, and strong developer experience, and success is measured by the productivity of the teams who depend on it. Our ideal candidate combines solid distributed systems engineering with operational maturity, clear communication, and a habit of mentoring those earlier in their careers. The role reports to the Team Lead, Data Platform Engineering, and is based in Cape Town, hybrid, with two days per week in office.

The platform:

The platform has strong foundations: Scala and Spark pipelines processing TB-scale data, dozens of managed data connectors, Airflow on Astronomer for orchestration, a mature dbt transformation layer, and BigQuery as the core analytical warehouse. You'll also have room to shape the platform's next chapter: modernising parts of the compute stack, and building out governance frameworks, data contracts, SLOs, observability, cost management, and data quality monitoring within your domain.

What You'll Do:

End-to-end domain ownership: Own platform components and a pipeline domain end-to-end, including design, implementation, reliability, performance, and cost. Design and build scalable ETL/ELT and streaming pipelines using Spark/Dataproc, Kafka, and Pub/Sub. Integrate diverse sources into BigQuery and other stores. Build modular, fault-tolerant components with graceful schema evolution.

Infrastructure & performance tuning: Configure and maintain core platform infrastructure as code, including Dataproc, Kafka, Airflow/Astronomer, BigQuery, and Cloud Storage. Tune performance and cost through query optimisation, partitioning, and resource configuration. Tune streaming configurations for throughput and reliability.

Reliability & incident response: Own and track SLOs for freshness, success, and latency. Implement monitoring, alerting, and data quality checks. Participate in on-call as a Tier 2 responder, troubleshooting and resolving incidents independently.

Security, governance & self-service: Implement security and governance by design, including access control, secrets, encryption, audit logging, lineage, and retention. Build self-service capabilities and paved roads for analytics engineers, analysts, and data scientists.

Engineering craft & documentation: Write clean, well-tested code with CI/CD and current runbooks and architecture docs. Use AI coding assistants while holding the same quality and review standards.

Mentorship & communication: Mentor Associate Data Platform Engineers through pairing and code review. Communicate platform trade-offs clearly and contribute to platform standards and data contracts.

What You Have:

Preferred Requirements:

3 to 5 years of experience in data platform, data engineering, or backend/distributed systems engineering, including ownership of production systems at TB-scale, or systems carrying stringent SLAs, multiple downstream consumers, or compliance requirements

Strong Python, plus production experience in a JVM language, with the ability to write production-quality code with proper error handling, logging, and testing. Scala is our primary pipeline language: if you don't have it yet, you'll need a real appetite to become strong in it

Hands-on depth in either distributed batch processing (Spark: DataFrames, Spark SQL, partitioning, shuffles, fault tolerance) or streaming (Kafka or Pub/Sub: producers, consumers, topics, partitions, stream processing patterns), with working familiarity of the other

Advanced SQL, including complex queries, window functions, CTEs, and query optimisation

Experience with workflow orchestration such as Airflow: scheduling, dependencies, retry logic, and workflow coordination

Working fluency with a major cloud platform, ideally GCP (BigQuery, Dataproc, Cloud Storage, Pub/Sub)

Solid engineering and operational practice: Git, CI/CD, automated testing, code review, monitoring, alerting, and incident response including on-call

Security and governance practice in data systems: access control, secrets management, encryption, and least-privilege design

Clear written and verbal communication for a distributed team, plus some experience or aptitude for mentoring less experienced engineers

Nice to Have (Advantageous) Requirements:

Infrastructure as code (Terraform or equivalent) and automated deployment

Experience migrating legacy big-data platforms onto cloud-native alternatives

Familiarity with dbt, Looker, or semantic layer concepts, and with dbt orchestration through Astronomer Cosmos

Functional Scala patterns (cats-effect and the Typelevel ecosystem), or JVM tuning exposure such as garbage collection, memory management, and thread pools

Observability tooling such as Grafana, Datadog, or Cloud Monitoring

Experience with Dataflow (Apache Beam), SingleStore, or BigTable

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field is a plus

Experience in the digital marketing technology industry is a plus

listings.description:
About impact.com:

impact.com is the world’s leading commerce partnership marketing platform, transforming the way businesses grow by enabling them to discover, manage, and scale partnerships across the entire customer journey. From affiliates and influencers to content publishers, brand ambassadors, and customer advocates, impact.com empowers brands to drive trusted, performance-based growth through authentic relationships. Today, over 5,000 global brands - including Walmart, Uber, Shopify, Lenovo, and Fanatics - rely on impact.com to power more than 350,000 partnerships that deliver measurable business results.

Your Role at impact.com:

We're seeking a Data Scientist to help build the next generation of recommendation systems powering our partnership automation platform. Our ecosystem connects a rich set of entities—advertisers, media publishers, creators, products, and consumers—and the relationships between them are where the real value lives. Your work will help surface the right partnerships, the right products, and the right content across this network at scale.

You'll contribute to evolving our recommender stack toward a graph-based architecture leveraging semantic embeddings of entities and their relationships, applying cutting-edge techniques in representation learning, graph ML, and retrieval. The system needs to serve recommendations both in batch and real time, respond to dynamic user inputs, drive measurable value for end users across the platform, and remain reliable as the ecosystem grows.

This role is hands-on and end-to-end. You'll own modeling and experimentation work for a defined area of the recommendation stack—from problem framing through productionization—in close partnership with Engineering, Product, MLOps, and Business Stakeholders. You're expected to bring (or actively develop) ML engineering chops so you can take a solution from prototype to production, and to be a relentless user of AI coding agents to multiply your output and accelerate iteration.

What You'll Do:

Core Responsibilities

Multi-entity recommendations across the partnership graph

Design, build, and evaluate recommendation models that operate across heterogeneous entities—advertisers, publishers, creators, products, and consumers—and the relationships between them. Frame problems in terms of the partnership graph and apply techniques appropriate to each surface, including candidate generation, ranking, reranking, and personalization.

Graph-based modeling & semantic embeddings

Contribute to evolving our architecture toward graph-based approaches: learn semantic embeddings of entities and relationships, apply graph neural networks or attention aware graph transformer models where they add value, and build representations that generalize across surfaces and use cases. Stay current with cutting-edge techniques in graph ML, representation learning, and modern recommender architectures, and bring relevant ideas into the platform.

Batch and real-time serving

Build models and pipelines that serve recommendations in both batch and real-time contexts. Partner with Engineering on retrieval infrastructure, vector search, feature stores, and low-latency serving patterns. Make pragmatic tradeoffs between model sophistication, latency, cost, and freshness based on the surface and use case.

End-to-end ML delivery & ML engineering

Own the full lifecycle of your work: data and feature design, model development, evaluation, launch, monitoring, and iteration. Build production-grade pipelines, write code that other engineers can extend, and partner with MLOps on reproducibility, observability, and reliability. Use AI coding agents aggressively to accelerate prototyping, refactoring, debugging, and shipping—we expect this to be a core part of how you work, not an occasional aid.

Experimentation & measurement

Design offline evaluation (offline replay, counterfactual evaluation, holdout sets) and online experiments (A/B tests, holdouts, interleaving) to quantify model impact. Apply appropriate statistical methods, recognize common pitfalls in recommender evaluation (position bias, feedback loops, selection effects), and translate results into clear recommendations for product and engineering partners.

Cross-functional collaboration

Work closely with Product, Engineering, and Business Stakeholders to translate platform goals into measurable model outcomes. Communicate findings, tradeoffs, and recommendations clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences. Document your work so that models, features, and decisions are understandable and reproducible by others.

What You Bring:

3+ years of experience in data science / applied ML, with a track record of shipping production models that delivered measurable user or business impact.

Strong Python and SQL skills; experience working with large-scale data and distributed compute (Spark/Databricks or equivalent).

Hands-on experience building recommendation or ranking systems—candidate generation, learning-to-rank, retrieval and reranking, or implicit feedback modeling.

Experience with embeddings and representation learning for users, items, content, or other entities.

ML engineering capability (or strong willingness and demonstrated ability to develop it): you can build, ship, and maintain production pipelines—not just prototypes in notebooks.

Strong experimentation skills: designing and analyzing A/B tests, interpreting results, and communicating findings to stakeholders.

Relentless user of AI coding agents in your day-to-day workflow, with a clear sense of where they accelerate you and where they don't.

Insatiable curiosity about new techniques, architectures, and tools—and a track record of teaching yourself things quickly. You read papers, try new tools, and bring ideas back to the team.

Strong problem-solving instincts and the ability to operate with growing autonomy in ambiguous, evolving spaces.

Preferred / Nice to have

Experience with graph-based ML: graph neural networks (KGAT, transformers or similar), graph-aware retrieval, or knowledge graph embeddings.

Experience with modern deep learning recommender architectures (two-tower, sequence/transformer-based recommenders, multi-task ranking).

Familiarity with vector search and vector databases (FAISS, ScaNN, Vespa, Milvus, or similar) and approximate nearest neighbor methods.

Experience with real-time ML serving, feature stores (Feast, Tecton, or equivalent), and low-latency inference patterns.

Exposure to contextual bandits, reinforcement learning, or off-policy evaluation in recommendation settings.

Familiarity with PyTorch/TensorFlow and PyTorch Geometric / DGL for graph workloads.

Familiarity with GCP (Vertex AI, BigQuery, Cloud Run) and/or mature MLOps practices (CI/CD for ML, monitoring, drift detection).

Experience in adtech, martech, e-commerce, or two-sided/multi-sided marketplace recommendations.

What Sets You Apart

You think in terms of user and business outcomes, not just model metrics, and you connect modeling choices to real value delivered through the platform.

You're rigorous about measurement but pragmatic about shipping—able to deliver MVPs and iteratively evolve them into durable production systems.

You're a relentless learner. New papers, new tools, new architectures—you find them, try them, and figure out where they fit. You don't wait to be told what to learn.

You use AI coding agents like a power user: they're a force multiplier in your hands, not a crutch.

You have engineering instincts—you care about code quality, system design, and operability, not just model performance.

You're comfortable with messy data, noisy feedback, edge cases, and ambiguous problem spaces, and you excel at iterative improvement.

You bring clarity to ambiguity, communicate clearly across functions, and help teams align on tradeoffs.

Consistent with applicable law, compensation will be determined based on the skills, qualifications, and experience of the applicant along with the requirements of the position, and the Company reserves the right to modify this pay range at any time.

listings.description:
About impact.com

At impact.com we are passionate about our people, our technology, and are obsessed with customer success. Working together enables us to grow rapidly, win, and serve the largest brands in the world. We use cutting edge technology to solve real-world problems for our clients and continue to pull ahead of the pack as the leading SaaS platform for businesses to automate their partnerships and grow their revenue like never before. We have an entrepreneurial spirit and a culture where ambition and curiosity is rewarded. If you are looking to join a team where your opinion is valued, your contributions are noticed, and enjoy working with fun and talented people from all over the world, then this is the place for you! 

impact.com, the world’s leading partnership management platform, is transforming the way businesses manage and optimize all types of partnerships—including traditional rewards affiliates, influencers, commerce content publishers, B2B, and more. The company’s powerful, purpose-built platform makes it easy for businesses to create, manage, and scale an ecosystem of partnerships with the brands and communities that customers trust to make purchases, get information, and entertain themselves at home, at work, or on the go. To learn more about how impact.com’s technology platform and partnerships marketplace is driving revenue growth for global enterprise brands such as Walmart, Uber, Shopify, Lenovo, L’Oreal and Fanatics visit www.impact.com.

Your Role at impact.com

As we grow across APAC and beyond, we’re looking for a Global Payroll Specialist based in Malaysia to help us ensure our people are paid accurately, on time, and in compliance across several countries. You’ll work closely with our international Finance, HR, and Ops teams, acting as a trusted expert for all things payroll. This role is ideal for someone who’s experienced, detail-obsessed, and confident working independently across borders. You’ll support countries like Malaysia, Singapore, China, and Australia, with opportunities to grow your expertise across more regions as we expand. If you love making complex systems run smoothly, thrive in a global team, and want to play a key role in supporting our people, this role is for you.

What You’ll Do

Manage the day-to-day end-to-end payroll process for multiple APAC countries (Malaysia, Australia, Singapore, China, Japan) ensuring payroll is processed accurately, on time, and in accordance with local requirements.

Take ownership of payroll issues through to resolution and proactively identify opportunities to improve
the efficiency, accuracy, and effectiveness of day-to-day payroll processes.

Maintain accurate payroll records and documentation, following established payroll processes, controls, and confidentiality requirements.

Support statutory payroll requirements and submissions, ensuring relevant deadlines are tracked and met.

Provide clear and responsive payroll support to employees, resolving queries within agreed SLAs and prioritizing urgent or time-sensitive matters.

Prepare and review payroll reports, payment files, reconciliations, and other payroll documentation required for each payroll cycle.

Work closely with payroll vendors to provide accurate inputs, review payroll outputs, follow up on issues, and ensure agreed payroll timelines are met.

Coordinate closely with HR and Finance to ensure payroll data is accurately reflected between Workday, payroll software, and payroll accounting.

Perform payroll checks, reconciliations, and variance analysis to identify and resolve discrepancies before payroll is finalized.

Collect, review, and process payroll inputs including new hires, terminations, salary changes, bonuses, commissions, benefits, deductions, and banking changes.

What You'll Bring:

3+ years of payroll experience, ideally with exposure to multi-country payroll across APAC.

High level of integrity, discretion, and professionalism when handling confidential payroll and employee information.

A proactive and positive working attitude, with a willingness to learn, support the team, and look for practical ways to improve processes.

Experience with payroll software and good working knowledge of Excel or Google Sheets, including reconciliations and data checks.

A strong sense of ownership and accountability, with the ability to follow tasks through to completion and escalate issues when needed.

Responsive and reliable, with the ability to manage employee and stakeholder queries within agreed SLAs.

Strong organizational and time-management skills, with a clear sense of urgency around payroll deadlines.

Strong attention to detail and accuracy, with the ability to work confidently with payroll data and identify discrepancies.

Good understanding of payroll processes, statutory requirements, and payroll timelines.

listings.title: Principal Engineer, Quality Platform
listings.description:
The Company:

impact.com is the world’s leading commerce partnership marketing platform, transforming the way businesses grow by enabling them to discover, manage, and scale partnerships across the entire customer journey. From affiliates and influencers to content publishers, brand ambassadors, and customer advocates, impact.com empowers brands to drive trusted, performance-based growth through authentic relationships. Its award-winning products—Performance (affiliate), Creator (influencer), and Advocate (customer referral)—unify every type of partner into one integrated platform. As consumers increasingly rely on recommendations from people and communities they trust, impact.com helps brands show up where it matters most. Today, over 5,000 global brands, including Walmart, Uber, Shopify, Lenovo, L’Oréal, and Fanatics, rely on impact.com to power more than 225,000 partnerships that deliver measurable business results.

Your Role at impact.com:

Quality at impact.com is an engineering problem: the platforms, frameworks and AI agents that let teams test well at speed. Today that work is spread across a team, with promising prototypes and no dedicated owner. As our Principal Software Engineer for the QA Platform, you'll be that owner. You’ll build our CLIs, MCPs, and full-stack web apps used by hundreds of users and thousands of agents. The ideal candidate would be one of the founders or principal engineers at Playwright, Browserstack, Checksum, SauceLabs or similar dev tools companies. You'll set the technical direction for the QA platform: the frameworks, shared standards, quality context and AI agents that QA engineers and developers across our product groups rely on. You'll decide which prototypes become platforms and which are retired. This is a software engineering role, not a testing role: you'll build for QA the way a platform team builds for developers, as a multiplier for teams rather than a release gate. At this level you lead by doing. You're a hands-on individual contributor with no direct reports, trusted to take on ambiguous problems, make consequential technical decisions, and bring people along through influence rather than authority.

What You'll Do:

1. Set the direction

Own the multi-quarter technical vision, architecture and roadmap for the QA platform.

Turn ambiguous, cross-team quality problems into clear technical direction, including ones nobody has fully defined yet.

Decide what to build, buy, adopt or retire, and when a problem deserves something purpose-built.

2. Build, hands-on

Write code and prototype the hardest parts yourself, especially where the problem is new or the risk is high.

Own what you ship in production: its reliability, security and cost.

Bring AI into how we test where it measurably helps, and show the evidence when it doesn't.

3. Raise the bar and bring people with you

Define what good looks like for quality engineering at impact.com, including for AI-assisted work, and hold that line across teams.

Lead technically without authority: set standards, review designs and code, and mentor engineers across QA Enablement and the QA chapter.

Partner with engineering leadership, and with the Engineering Enablement PM, who owns rollout and adoption. You own technical readiness and the evidence that the platform helps.

Essential requirements:

A Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

Typically 10+ years of professional software engineering, including designing and delivering complex systems.

A track record of setting technical direction across several teams, whatever your title.

You've built platforms, frameworks or developer tools that other engineers adopted and relied on.

Deep, hands-on backend and infrastructure engineering: you design, build and run distributed, highly available production systems, and you still write code.

Expert in at least one backend language, and able to work across others.

You've built and shipped LLM- or agent-based tools, and can show how you measured whether their output was good enough to trust. You use AI coding tools every day.

Experience in test infrastructure, developer productivity or CI/CD at scale. You don't need a testing background, but you understand what makes tests fast and trusted.

Clear technical writing: design docs and decisions that other teams act on, and explanations non-technical audiences can follow.

Nice-to-have requirements:

Building eval infrastructure for LLM or agent output, or testing other non-deterministic systems.

Giving AI agents the context they need, for example through MCP's and CLI's.

Moving teams from fragmented tooling onto a shared standard.

Enough front-end skill to ship usable internal tools.

Our stack includes Java and Python services on GCP and Kubernetes, with TypeScript and Playwright for test and UI work. Experience with them helps, but isn't required. The years are a guide, not a gate: what you've built and the scope you've owned matter more. If you've done most of this at a comparable level, apply.

Benefits and Perks

At impact.com, we believe that when you're happy and fulfilled, you do your best work. That's why we've built a benefits package that supports your well-being, growth, and work-life balance.

Flexible Working: Our Responsible PTO policy means you can take the time off you need to rest and recharge. We're committed to a positive work-life balance and provide a flexible environment that allows you to be happy and fulfilled in both your career and your personal life.

Health and Wellness: Your well-being is a priority. Our mental health and wellness benefit includes up to 12 fully covered therapy/coaching sessions per year, with additional dependent coverage. We also offer a monthly gym reimbursement policy to support your physical health.

A Stake in Our Growth: We offer Restricted Stock Units (RSUs) as part of our total compensation, giving you a stake in the company's growth with a 3-year vesting schedule, pending Board approval.

Investing in Your Growth: We're committed to your continuous learning. Take advantage of our free Coursera subscription and our PXA courses.

Parental Support: We offer a generous parental leave policy, 26 weeks of fully paid leave for the primary caregiver and 13 weeks fully paid leave for the secondary caregiver.

Your Role at impact.com:

We’re hiring a technical Product Manager for the Action Processing (AP) and Contracting Squad — one of impact.com’s most foundational domains: how brands and partners define terms, commissions, lists, and contract workflows that power revenue on the platform.

This is a step up from associate-level execution. Ownership and delivery of value / outcomes are the core of this role: you own feature sets end-to-end, define what success looks like, and are accountable for shipped results — not only clear tickets and on-time delivery.

You have already made the shift to building with AI: you use agents and modern AI tooling to ship real artifacts (specs, prototypes, analyses, internal tools, personal projects). You’ll partner with a Senior Product Manager and Engineering with meaningful independence: you lead specs, own prioritization within your scope, and bring recommendations — not only options to escalate.

What You'll Do:

Ownership, outcomes & delivery

Own feature development for Action Processing (AP) and Contracting Squad initiatives (e.g. terms/commission behaviors, list and audience rules, contract workflows, and customer-driven requests).

Define success up front (metrics / OKRs), ship, and follow through on outcomes — adoption, quality, rework reduction, or business impact — not just output.

Write high-quality customer and business requirements that reduce rework and protect engineering focus.

Develop Markdown requirements that live adjacent to the GitHub repo (versioned next to eng context, not only in Confluence/docs silos); lead pre-spec and spec reviews and drive release prioritization. Optimize for short time from ask → usable draft → eng-ready.

Partner with Engineering through build: surface risks early; make crisp tradeoffs under incomplete information and own the recommendation.

Technical product craft & AI-native building

Operate as a technical PM in a systems-heavy domain: map system behavior, data flows, edge cases, and cross-squad dependencies with limited coaching.

Use AI tools and agents as a core part of how you build — at work or in personal projects — to draft and pressure-test specs fast, synthesize research, prototype flows, explore edge cases, and accelerate analysis. AI should cut time to a good requirement, not inflate polish time.

Walk through concrete AI-assisted builds you’ve shipped (prototypes, scripts, internal tools, product experiments, side projects): what you built, how agents/tools fit, what you validated, and how quickly others could react.

Run analyses from source data and convert findings into insights, conclusions, and recommendations that drive prioritization and outcome tracking.

Squad partnership & operational excellence

Keep a clear, healthy backlog (ticket clarity, prioritization hygiene, meeting facilitation, and request triage).

Sequence work with Engineering leads; facilitate working sessions across Engineering, Design, Customer Success / Technical Services, and adjacent PMs.

Hold alignment touchpoints that keep priorities clear and reduce coordination drag.

Roadmap, go-to-market & stakeholders

Shape and communicate the roadmap within your owned scope; connect near-term delivery to outcomes the business cares about.

Partner with Product Marketing on go-to-market for your launches.

Involve the right stakeholders; escalate only when needed — default is a clear recommendation with tradeoffs.

Contribute to vision and strategic initiatives in the domain through owned delivery, not only input.

How we work

Build deep fluency in AP & Contracting mechanics and how they connect to the broader platform.

Build trusted working relationships; brainstorm constructively; participate actively in team forums.

Demonstrate impact.com’s Operating Principles consistently (customer focus, ownership, trust, getting the right stuff done, innovate & simplify, get better every day).

What You’ll Bring:

Several years of product management experience (typically 3+) with evidence of independent feature ownership and delivered outcomes in a technical or systems-heavy product — not only participation on a squad.

Proven ownership mindset: you can point to features or initiatives you owned end-to-end, how you defined success, and what changed after ship (metrics, quality, adoption, or business impact).

Background in engineering or computer science — through degree and/or prior hands-on engineering experience.

Technical PM profile: you have already operated in systems-heavy domains; you dig into how systems work, map cross-squad dependencies, partner fluently with engineers, and write requirements that reflect real constraints — not only customer asks.

AI-native building with a portfolio you can walk through (work or personal): real artifacts built with AI tools/agents (specs, prototypes, scripts, internal tools, experiments). Demonstrated habit, not an interest area.

Fast time to value on requirements. You shape usable Markdown requirements quickly and iterate with eng and stakeholders — short cycle from ask to eng-ready draft.

Bias to execution and outcomes: you prioritize ruthlessly, close loops, and ship value — not activity.

Business economics mindset: you understand how product decisions grow the business (especially GTV / monetization), not just how to ship features.

Strong written craft in Markdown requirements that sit adjacent to the GitHub repo: specs, acceptance criteria, and lightweight PRDs engineers can use in context.

Experience working with Customer Success, Technical Services, support, or field teams on triage and prioritization.

Comfortable running analyses from source data and converting findings into insights, conclusions, and recommendations that inform prioritization and success metrics — not only consuming dashboards or reports produced by others.

Clear judgment under incomplete information: you protect engineering focus and default to recommendations with tradeoffs, not open-ended escalation.

Customer empathy for brands and partners navigating contracting, action processing, terms, and monetization workflows.

listings.description:
About impact.com

impact.com is the world’s leading commerce partnership marketing platform, transforming the way businesses grow by enabling them to discover, manage, and scale partnerships across the entire customer journey. From affiliates and influencers to content publishers, brand ambassadors, and customer advocates, impact.com empowers brands to drive trusted, performance-based growth through authentic relationships. Its award-winning products—Performance (affiliate), Creator (influencer), and Advocate (customer referral)—unify every type of partner into one integrated platform. As consumers increasingly rely on recommendations from people and communities they trust, impact.com helps brands show up where it matters most. Today, over 5,000 global brands, including Walmart, Uber, Shopify, Lenovo, L’Oréal, and Fanatics, rely on impact.com to power more than 225,000 partnerships that deliver measurable business results.

About the Role

We're seeking a Technical Product Manager to own the foundational data layer that powers our benchmarking, recommendation, classification, and personalization systems. In this role, you'll own the operational and structural integrity of our taxonomy ecosystem — spanning partner/brand/product/content classification, proprietary vertical taxonomies, and the pipeline discipline that gets new taxonomies safely into production. This is a role that demands precision, technical fluency, and comfort with ambiguity in messy real-world data — not roadmap ownership for external-facing products. You'll spend your time in classification logic, data quality audits, and the mechanics of promoting data assets from prototype (BigQuery) to production (SingleStore), working directly inside the dbt-and-pull-request workflow alongside engineering. Your work will directly influence the accuracy, consistency, and trustworthiness of the data foundation that every downstream product (search, scoring, recommendations, reporting) depends on.

Core Responsibilities

Taxonomy design & maintenance

Own and evolve classification structures for partners, brands, products, and content.

Design and maintain the GEO prompt category taxonomy.

Build proprietary product taxonomies for verticals not covered by Google Merchant Center — financial services, B2B, and travel.

Own the action tracker taxonomy and audience segmentation taxonomy.

Collaborate with category and domain experts to refine taxonomy definitions, resolve edge cases, and adapt structures as new entity types emerge.

Data quality & hygiene

Conduct deep-dive audits into taxonomy coverage, consistency, and correctness across systems and entity types.

Define and track data quality KPIs (classification accuracy, coverage gaps, taxonomy drift, schema compliance) and drive remediation when they slip.

Root-cause and resolve systematic misclassification issues at scale, not just one-off tickets.

Build monitoring and alerting to proactively surface taxonomy or data quality degradation before it reaches downstream consumers.

Prototype-to-production pipeline (co-owned)

Co-own the developer playbook for promoting new taxonomies, metrics, and data outputs from prototype (BigQuery) to production (SingleStore).

Work directly inside the pull-request workflow — reviewing schema changes, validating classification logic, and coordinating promotion timing with engineering.

Ensure new taxonomy work is production-ready: documented, tested, versioned, and maintainable by others after you've moved on to the next thing.

Insights & stakeholder communication

Translate taxonomy and data quality findings into clear, actionable recommendations for engineering, DS, and business stakeholders.

Build and maintain reporting on taxonomy health and coverage across verticals.

Partner with data producers and consumers to resolve classification conflicts and taxonomy ambiguity.

Requirements:

Required

4+ years in a technical Product Management, data Product Management, or data governance role, with direct ownership of a taxonomy or classification system at scale.

Working fluency in SQL and demonstrated comfort operating inside a dbt workflow — reading models, understanding lineage, reviewing pull requests. You don't need to write production dbt code daily, but you can't be intimidated by it.

Demonstrated experience designing or maintaining a taxonomy or classification system, ideally across multiple verticals or entity types.

Experience with BigQuery and/or SingleStore, or similar warehouse-to-serving-layer promotion patterns.

Strong written documentation habits — taxonomy decisions need to be legible to engineering, DS, and downstream consumers, not just to you.

Comfort with ambiguity in messy, real-world data — you find edge cases interesting, not annoying. 

Education: Bachelor's in a quantitative field (CS, Statistics, Math, Engineering, or similar); Master's/PhD preferred.

Preferred / Nice to have

Experience with GMC (Google Merchant Center) taxonomy or similar commerce/product classification standards.

Background in a marketplace, affiliate, or partner-ecosystem business where multi-sided classification (advertisers/publishers/products) is core.

Familiarity with entity resolution, deduplication, or classification modeling concepts (you don't need to build the models, but you need to speak the language with the DS team that does).

Exposure to master data management (MDM) or data governance practices.

What sets you apart

Taxonomy obsession: You care deeply about classification correctness and understand how a sloppy taxonomy cascades into bad recommendations, bad reporting, and eroded trust downstream.

Operational rigor over roadmap glamour: You get more satisfaction from a clean audit and a correctly resolved edge case than from a shiny new feature launch.

Pipeline fluency: You're not afraid of dbt, PRs, or the prototype-to-production handoff — you see it as core to the job, not someone else's problem.

Detective instincts: You love digging into messy classification data, finding systemic patterns, and tracing root causes rather than patching symptoms.

Stakeholder fluency without scope creep: You can translate technical taxonomy work for non-technical stakeholders while staying disciplined about what is and isn't in your lane.

A Stake in Our Growth: We offer Restricted Stock Units (RSUs) as part of our total compensation, giving you a stake in the company's growth with a 3-year vesting schedule, pending Board approval.

Investing in Your Growth: We’re committed to your continuous learning. Take advantage of our free Coursera subscription and our PXA courses.

Your Role at impact.com:

The QA Chapter Lead sets the quality bar across our IO and AI groups and makes engineering teams the owners of it. This is a leadership role built on influence rather than a separate reporting line: you raise the standard of quality by shaping how teams design, build, and ship, by coaching engineers to own testing end to end, and by building the tooling and evaluation systems that make quality the path of least resistance. You will treat quality as an engineering discipline embedded in every team, not as a downstream gate a dedicated QA person is responsible for. The role deliberately spans two very different delivery contexts. The IO group builds deterministic platform software: integrations, ETL pipelines, APIs, and the performance and security concerns that come with them. The AI group builds non-deterministic, agentic products where correctness, safety, cost, and latency are all quality dimensions and where traditional test scripts do not apply. You will build one quality discipline that works across both.

What You'll Do:

As a QA Lead for the platform group, you will lead a critical function focused on both the technical infrastructure and the human element of Quality Assurance. 

Your responsibilities will include:

1. Set the quality bar and the operating model

Define what "good" looks like across both groups, and make engineers the owners of that bar rather than the QA function.

Shift quality upstream, from a downstream gate into how teams scope, design, and build, so that testing is part of engineering rather than a phase after it. 

Establish quality signals teams actually use to make decisions (escaped defects, mean time to detect, confidence to ship, change failure rate) over vanity metrics like raw test-case counts.

Drive continuous improvement of how the groups engineer for quality, and retire practices that no longer earn their keep.

2. Lead the chapter, not a QA queue

Grow a cross-group chapter and community of practice for quality engineering spanning IO and AI, aligning standards without centralising the work.

Coach engineers to own testing for their own work, increasingly with agents doing the heavy lifting. Lead through standards, reviews, pairing, and reusable patterns rather than by running a separate QA backlog that work is handed off to.

Raise the floor for everyone: onboarding, patterns, reusable harnesses, and the internal enablement that lets any engineer test well by default.

Provide technical mentorship and feedback that grows quality capability inside the engineering teams.

3. Quality engineering in the agentic age

Treat agents as first-class contributors to testing: generating tests, test data, and exploratory coverage, triaging failures, and widening coverage, with humans designing the harnesses, guardrails, and reviews that keep them honest.

Build the evaluation systems for AI products: evals, regression suites for non-deterministic output, and safety, hallucination, and guardrail testing, alongside strong classic automation for the platform.

Own the tooling, harnesses, and CI/CD guardrails that make the quality bar automatic rather than a matter of individual diligence.

Stay ahead of where AI-assisted testing and agentic engineering are going, and bring the useful parts back into both groups.

4. Test strategy across two contexts

For the IO platform: functional, regression, integration, performance, and security testing, with strong automation and quality gates in CI/CD.

For AI products: eval-driven testing for non-deterministic and agentic behaviour, including prompt and behaviour regression, safety, and cost and latency as first-class quality signals.

Ensure risk-based coverage in both, so effort follows blast radius rather than spreading evenly.

Make release readiness a team decision backed by shared signals, with your discipline setting the standard for what "ready" means.

5. Influence and collaboration

Partner with Engineering Leads and Product Managers to move quality left and to design in testability and clear acceptance criteria from the start.

Communicate quality posture, risks, and the signals behind them to stakeholders, and inform go/no-go decisions with data while ownership stays with the teams.

Partner with QA platform and enable the ability to evaluate and adopt next-generation tools and techniques for the discipline.

Essential requirements: 

5+ years of experience in Quality Assurance and/or Software Development

Engineering in Test (SDET) background, with a strong background in test automation and platform development.

Champion of Quality: Proven track record of owning and upholding the absolute standard of software quality for an entire group or department.

Leadership through influence: a track record of raising quality across teams you did not directly manage, by setting standards and coaching rather than by owning a central QA queue.

A multiplier, not a gatekeeper: proven ability to make other engineers own and raise quality, so the bar holds without you personally testing everything or acting as the release gate.

Agentic AI expertise: Practical familiarity with putting AI at the forefront to improve engineering workflows, including experience with MCPs, Agents and Agent Skills, and utilizing/building testing harnesses.

Testing AI systems: practical experience evaluating non-deterministic or agentic products, for example building eval harnesses and regression suites for LLM or agent behaviour, and testing for safety and guardrail failures.

Infrastructure foundations: strong understanding of cloud ecosystems, containerisation (Docker), ETL pipelines, and API endpoints.

Deep expertise in testing methodologies, tools, and frameworks (e.g. Playwright, Selenium, TestRail, API testing, CI/CD integration).

Excellent communication and influence, with the ability to align engineers, product, and leadership around a quality bar they choose to own.

Proactive, first-principles mindset, always looking for ways to improve quality, flow, and developer experience rather than to add process.

Nice-to-have requirements: 

Experience leading test framework or tooling migrations.

Familiarity with OWASP guidelines and security testing tools.

Interest in SRE principles and treating reliability as a quality concern.

Experience embedding quality practices into teams that had none, or moving a team off a dedicated-QA model.

Your Role at impact.com:

As a Quality Assurance Engineer in the Finance Invoicing Squad at impact.com, you will treat our software architecture as a dynamic, living system, directly aligning your testing strategies with critical financial outcomes and long-term customer value. You will leverage high adaptability and numerical logic to move fast, avoid analysis paralysis, and build automated and manual testing structures that scale seamlessly as our platform grows.

Operating in an entrepreneurial, high-accountability, blame-free culture where ambition, curiosity, and diverse perspectives are rewarded, you will utilize Playwright, SQL, and API testing methodologies to deliver high-quality software. This role carries a unique dual mandate: providing direct influence through every phase of the feature delivery workflow while ensuring the persistent health of our invoicing and ledger infrastructures. You will optimize for future system health with a zero-tolerance stance on data inconsistency, delivery delays, or hidden single points of failure.

What You'll Do:

Automation Engineering & Scalability

Playwright Framework Expansion: Design, configure, and scale a modular automated regression pack using Playwright to validate complex end-to-end user billing journeys, invoices, payment routing flows, and overall system interfaces.

Predictive Pipeline Execution: Ensure daily test suites run smoothly on schedule. Efficiently debug test failures using execution traces, video recordings, and artifacts to isolate backend root causes from superficial symptoms.

Code Review & Continuity: Review and action pull requests within the QA repository, ensuring that the automated test framework remains thoroughly documented with a strict focus on system continuity.

Cloud Infrastructure Emulation: Utilize cloud testing platforms to perform targeted manual and visual mobile web audits, evaluating layout boundaries and touch thresholds across diverse physical and virtual device profiles.

AI-Augmented Testing: Leverage LLM-based tooling and coding assistants to accelerate test authoring, generate synthetic data for edge-case coverage, and rapidly triage log signals. Crucially, you will apply a "verify-first" mental model—using AI for velocity, but applying deterministic, human-led verification for all financial calculations where accuracy is non-negotiable.

Data, Analysis & Manual Testing Mastery

Rigorous Test Planning: Review product designs and technical requirements throughout the SDLC to ensure they are correct, unambiguous, and verifiable, proactively recommending architectural corrections to engineers.

Abstract Problem Solving: Analyze ambiguous user stories, ledger requirements, and system profiles to break down complex architectures into detailed test plans containing explicit functional, integration, regression, smoke, and sanity test cases.

Advanced SQL & Data Auditing: Apply data-driven judgment and advanced SQL queries to review 24-hour application and batch logs, performing deep schema validation and database integrity checks to target high-impact failure points.

Financial Data & Jurisdictional Verification: Apply strong numerical reasoning to stress-test complex financial calculations. Design testing scenarios using mathematical models to predict and verify tax documentation pipelines, transaction totals, rounding logic, multi-regional VAT requirements, and changing tax jurisdictions.

API & Integration Verification

Backend API Contract Testing: Validate RESTful APIs, backend endpoints, payload contracts, JSON/XML metadata responses, and authorization protocols.

Asynchronous Middleware Verification: Intercept, analyze, and mock internal and third-party event-driven webhooks, web services, and API retry mechanisms to ensure financial records match application states under abnormal conditions.

Vendor & Compatibility Audits: Partner with product development to evaluate operational constraints and conduct deep compatibility tests with vendor programs and third-party financial systems.

Operational Integrity & Decision Quality

App Health Monitoring: Run morning system health routines to verify transaction metrics, audit Application Performance Monitoring (APM) dashboards, track leading indicators, and ensure system anomalies are flagged immediately.

Batch Operational Auditing: Proactively identify, track, and report failed, delayed, or missing job executions (such as invoicing and automated balance imports) across core services (finance-app, finance-jobs, and payments-app).

listings.description:
About impact.com

impact.com is the world’s leading commerce partnership marketing platform, transforming the way businesses grow by enabling them to discover, manage, and scale partnerships across the entire customer journey. From affiliates and influencers to content publishers, brand ambassadors, and customer advocates, impact.com empowers brands to drive trusted, performance-based growth through authentic relationships. Its award-winning products—Performance (affiliate), Creator (influencer), and Advocate (customer referral)—unify every type of partner into one integrated platform. As consumers increasingly rely on recommendations from people and communities they trust, impact.com helps brands show up where it matters most. Today, over 5,000 global brands, including Walmart, Uber, Shopify, Lenovo, L’Oréal, and Fanatics, rely on impact.com to power more than 225,000 partnerships that deliver measurable business results.

Your Role at impact.com

impact.com's content team is expanding what we do with our first-party data and research — annual benchmark reports, survey-based studies, and the extended content built from them. We need a dedicated owner for this work: someone who can take findings from our research team and turn them into publish-ready content that tells a clear, arguable story, and who owns the end-to-end distribution of that content.

This role sits alongside our Marketing research team (Manager of Market Research and Analytics and a market research specialist) as the writing and content arm of impact.com's research function. You are not a researcher or an analyst — you're a content marketer with strong data literacy, who understands how to shape a dataset into a story for marketers, not for other analysts.

What You'll Do

End-to-end briefing and writing for all impact.com benchmark reports, survey-based studies, and first-party data content

Translating findings from research studies into content briefs, narrative angles, and a clear editorial spine — every report needs an arguable point of view, not just a summary of the data

Full ownership of distribution for research content: planning and executing email, social, and cross-channel promotion in partnership with the social and lifecycle teams

Judgment calls on when data should be visualized versus narrated — partnering with design and research to keep reports tight and visual-forward rather than dense and text-heavy

Maintaining editorial standards on all research content: thesis discipline, three-tier source attribution, citation integrity, and AIO/GEO compliance

Building and improving AI-assisted workflows (Claude, Gemini) for research content production

What Success Looks Like at 6 Months

You have taken complete ownership of briefing, crafting, and promoting research content—relieving our existing content marketing managers who handled this alongside their primary beats. Our research initiatives now feature a cohesive narrative voice backed by a scalable workflow, solidly positioning you as a core pillar within the research team.

What You Bring

5+ years of content marketing experience, ideally in B2B or SaaS

A portfolio that demonstrates strong, publish-ready long-form writing on data-driven topics (benchmark reports, whitepapers, industry studies)

Strong data literacy — comfortable reading survey results and analytics output and shaping them into a narrative, without needing to run the analysis yourself

Collaborative, not solo — work closely with Marketing Research to strike a balance, which means give-and-take, not full creative control over final framing.

Experience owning content distribution end-to-end, not just writing and handing off — from campaign coordination and design assets to sales/CS enablement, publication, and post-launch reporting and optimization

Comfort using AI tools (Claude, Gemini, or equivalent) as part of a daily writing and research workflow, with a genuine interest in building repeatable workflows with them

Excellent editorial judgment, including knowing when a chart should do the talking instead of another paragraph

Ability to translate what data means for different audiences — shaping the same finding into language that resonates

Willingness to build both muscles — data fluency and storytelling. We've seen writers learn to think in data and researchers learn to tell stories marketers gravitate toward; what matters is the openness to build if you’re missing one

Before You Apply

Review these three impact.com research pieces so you understand the kind of storytelling this role produces — we'll ask about them if you’re interviewed:

Prime Day Halo Effect

H1 2026 Consumer Shopping Trends

Black Friday Consumer Insights

Nice to Have

Solid grasp of data visualization best practices—no need to create charts yourself, but you instinctively recognize what makes graphics compelling and clear

Background in consumer research or practitioner-focused messaging—you know how to translate audience behavior into actionable narratives for modern marketers

Passionate about designing, testing, and refining custom AI-driven content generation processes

Proven track record of interviewing domain experts and weaving their insights directly into publication-ready copy

Working knowledge of survey methodology and the operational anatomy of quantitative research publications

listings.description:
About impact.com

impact.com is the world’s leading commerce partnership marketing platform, transforming the way businesses grow by enabling them to discover, manage, and scale partnerships across the entire customer journey.
